playbook.title: Channel — youtube.com/@brighamspianoservice
items: About 2,750 long-form videos and 475 Shorts (style pass on 2026-10-07). Restoration title formula: PREFIX: [Location] [Family] Heirloom [Year] [Maker] [Model/Type] Piano [Work type], plus an optional —hook!

Prefixes in the last 300 uploads: AFTER (77), BEFORE (46), IN THE SHOP (32), PROGRESS (19), BEFORE & AFTER (14), FOR SALE (14), DELIVERY and ON THE ROAD (4 each), Q&A (3). Heirloom appears in 67 of the last 100 long titles. The client's location usually goes first.

Work-type words: Restoration & Refinishing, Rebuild, Refurbishing & Refinishing, Full Restoration. Hooks go after an em dash and often end with !. Shorts reuse the long title and usually add ! (65 of the last 100 Shorts titles, versus 27 of 100 long titles).

Evergreen how-tos and stories are the long-form winners: Shane Bowle's Song and Story (138K), Rebuilding an Antique Piano: Before and After (63K), How To Fix A Squeaky Sustain Pedal (61K). Top Shorts are curiosity hooks: This piano's bridge was a disaster pt 1 (19K), What to do when your piano has a squeaking pedal (17K), Restoring Process: Piano Keys (14K), This is why pianos are so heavy (12K).

Recent medians: last 50 long videos about 300 views (median length 5:18); last 50 Shorts about 540 views. Among the last 150 Shorts, formula titles and plain-language titles share a median of about 670. BEFORE & AFTER Shorts lead that batch (1909 Friedrich Prein 1.6K, 1920 Gulbransen 1.4K).

playbook.title: Thumbnails
items: Brigham in a dark navy or black BLP button-up, smiling at the camera, standing beside the piano with a hand on it. The piano fills the other half.

Huge white stacked all-caps, 2–4 lines, flush and tight, heavy geometric sans (Montserrat ExtraBold/Black), soft dark drop shadow, no outline box. Text is a quirky story hook or a plain YEAR MAKER WORK label.

Before & After: a split frame with a small BEFORE / AFTER label in each half, or a red curved arrow. Sometimes a black BEFORE & AFTER banner with a gold serif sub-banner. Red circle badges and red arrows are the accent. Brand red #9e2020, near-black #121212, on warm shop wood.
Every Short gets a 1080x1920 cover in that same grammar: stacked white caps, a BEFORE/AFTER split, red accents.

playbook.title: Shorts spec
items: 1080x1920, 30–59 seconds. Hook in the first second: a big Montserrat Black line in the long-form thumbnail voice. Older Shorts had no hook text in the first second, small white serif captions low in the frame, and a plain near-black end card. New Shorts do not copy that.
Captions are phrase-level. The active word sits in a moving red rounded box. Keep captions between 55% and 75% of frame height, clear of the bottom 20% and the right-edge buttons.
Name card with a year count-up / speed ticker, for example 1911 → 2026 · 115 YRS. Every Short gets one.

Before → after swipes: as many as the footage allows, aim for 2–3 or more. Wipe only when the shots are feature-aligned. If the room, angle, or lens differs, crossfade. A misaligned wipe looks bad. Tag every swipe BEFORE/AFTER.
Let the playing run with no captions. Original audio only (Brigham talking, plus a little playing). No music bed and no copyrighted music (Content ID).

End card over continuing blurred footage, never a freeze. Website line is BrighamLarsonPianos.com (capital B, L, and P) on the end card, cover, captions, and description. Red button: SUBSCRIBE FOR MORE RESTORATIONS. Final screen also shows serial, brand, and year, for example 1911 STEINWAY · SN #154950.
QA before delivery: freezedetect and blackdetect, loudness about -14 LUFS, frame checks, and a video review.

playbook.title: Story, audiences, engagement
items: Heirloom / legacy: if Brigham or the notes mention heirloom, grandma, grandpa, family, mom, dad, generations, or legacy, emphasize it. Warm gold lower-third (FAMILY HEIRLOOM, GRANDMA'S PIANO, plus an italic story line), gold-highlighted caption words, and a slower softer beat. Brand means restoring musical legacy.

National brand: if the piano came from outside Utah, show an origin tag (SHIPPED FROM CALIFORNIA → OREM, UT) and, on the end card, ALL THE WAY FROM <STATE> → OREM, UT. Only a place a source states as the piano's origin. Never guess, and never infer it from a customer's address.

Family owned and operated: every end card carries a gold FAMILY OWNED & OPERATED tag. When footage, transcripts, or notes show family members, the owners' marriage partnership, or the family's entrepreneurial history, feature that with a lower-third, the hook, or the end card. Name someone only when a source names them.

Brigham the innovator: the nation's leading innovator using modern tech to restore old pianos while keeping old-world artisan craft. Fusion design, 3D-printed trim and action parts that cannot be replaced otherwise, CNC machining, and clever fixes. When that work is visible or stated, add an INNOVATION or MODERN FIX callout (one line on what the tech solves) plus the gold strap OLD-WORLD CRAFT + MODERN TECH. Traditional handwork (hammer reshaping, regulation, voicing, art preservation) gets a tip card so the contrast is on screen. Never claim a technique that is not visible or stated.
Capture Brigham's smiles and friendliness. Use those frames in the hook, as the reveal reaction, or under the end card.

Where the footage shows a process, add one tip callout: TECH TIP for technician-level facts, DID YOU KNOW? for enthusiasts and clients. One or two lines, accurate, drawn from what Brigham says or shows.

Audiences, and every Short names its main one in the notes: (1) piano technicians who want to learn from Brigham, (2) piano enthusiasts (history, makers, playing, transformations), (3) potential restoration clients (heirloom stories, results, trust, how to get started).

Engagement is currently very low. Every Short gets one specific comment question (an on-screen card, once, about 3–4 seconds, in a clean part of the shot and not over a swipe), a like/share/subscribe prompt, a pinned-comment question, a loop-friendly ending, and a link from the Short to the long video. Suggest series formats, cadence, cross-posting to IG Reels, TikTok, and Facebook, collabs, and replying to comments. Do not post those yourself.
